obligation: HIPAA breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise). Clock starts at discovery: the first day the breach is known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to the pharmacy (164.404(a)(2)). Counsel confirms whether the PMS vendor's discovery date counts as the pharmacy's
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected patient (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10 or more have out-of-date contact information)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity. The pharmacy keeps this duty even when the breach happens at the PMS vendor; it may ask the vendor in writing to send the notices for it

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Likely if the vendor's PMS data was taken: the PMS holds records for about 2,400 individuals

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: Breach affecting fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if under 500 (for example, a breach limited to the counter desktop's scanned prescriptions)

obligation: HIPAA media notice
trigger: Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the pharmacy (inbound)
trigger: The PMS vendor, cloud fax vendor, email and file suite vendor, or IT consultant discovers a breach of the pharmacy's PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery. The PMS vendor's BAA sets 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the main inbound notice in this scenario; ask the PMS vendor for written scope updates from day 0

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (includes medical history and treatment and health insurance identifiers)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach. A HIPAA-compliant notice is deemed compliant if the pharmacy timely provides a copy of that notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day clock; counsel confirms the deemed-compliance path

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Likely if the vendor's PMS data was taken

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Likely if the vendor's PMS data was taken (about 2,400 individuals)

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the pharmacy (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the pharmacy has a breach of security
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies to the PMS vendor; earlier than the HIPAA business associate clock

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 30 seasonal patients have addresses in other states; counsel checks each state

obligation: DEA report of an EPCS security incident
trigger: The pharmacy determines that an auditable event, or the attack on the pharmacy application, compromised or could have compromised the integrity of controlled substance prescription records
deadline: Within one business day of the determination
notify: The PMS vendor (as application service provider) and DEA (the local Diversion field office; counsel confirms the channel)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - a ransomware attack on the PMS vendor is very likely to meet this test

obligation: Stop processing EPCS when the application is non-compliant
trigger: The PMS vendor notifies the pharmacy that the application no longer meets the EPCS rule or has a non-compliance issue
deadline: Immediately; resume only after the vendor confirms compliance and updates are installed
notify: No outside notice; record the stop and restart in the incident log
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - ask the vendor directly whether the restored application is still compliant

obligation: CSOS private key loss or compromise
trigger: Loss, theft, or compromise of the owner's CSOS private key or its password is substantiated (for example, malware found on the counter desktop)
deadline: Within 24 hours of substantiation, by a revocation request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the counter desktop is compromised; apply for a new certificate afterward

obligation: PDMP reporting during downtime
trigger: Each controlled substance dispensed in Florida, including on paper during an outage
deadline: As soon as possible but no later than the close of the next business day after dispensing, unless the department approves an extension or exemption
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - enter paper-log dispensings through the PDMP web portal or ask the department for an extension before the deadline

obligation: Emergency oral Schedule II prescription not followed by a written prescription
trigger: A prescriber who gave an emergency oral authorization does not deliver the written prescription within 7 days
deadline: After the 7-day period passes
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if emergency oral authorizations are used during the outage

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected - the attack is on the vendor; applies if the pharmacy's own devices are ever held for ransom

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: Voluntary (no statutory deadline for this pharmacy)
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident affecting the pharmacy
deadline: As soon as practical (day 0 to 1)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended; reference the vendor's own report

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy terms
applies_at_this_tier: Only if coverage exists - no standalone cyber policy; ask the agent on day 0 whether the business owner's or professional liability policy has a cyber or business-interruption endorsement

obligation: PBM network agreement notices
trigger: Data security incident or inability to submit claims
deadline: Per each agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Check each agreement; not a legal duty under federal or Florida law

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Breach of personal health record information
deadline: Not applicable
applies_at_this_tier: No - the rule does not apply to HIPAA covered entities (16 CFR 318.1)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, an SBA-small pharmacy outside the sector criteria would not be covered

obligation: 42 CFR Part 2 breach
trigger: Breach of Part 2 records
deadline: Same as HIPAA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the pharmacy is not a Part 2 program (42 CFR 2.11)
